key_insight: UniTB combines physical priors with equivariant deep learning to predict Hamiltonians across diverse chemistries while constraining unphysical band shifts.
engineering_relevance: UniTB enables large-scale electronic-property screening, while UniTB-Flash reduces prior assembly to O(N) cost for N atoms.
method: Learn E(3)-equivariant corrections to a density-functional tight-binding prior.
Use prior-routed mixture-of-experts and a charge-equilibration head to support chemical generalization.
Bound band shifts through projection; accelerate computation with SO(2) GPU kernels and two-center tables.
evidence_signal: Trained on 29,242 crystals, UniTB achieved 0.48 meV matrix-element error on nonmagnetic test crystals spanning 68 elements; both variants reproduced DFT optical and conductivity results for amorphous Ge-Sb-Te without amorphous training data.
watch_item: UniTB-Flash preserved candidate rankings in the reported screening but delivered less accurate property values than UniTB, so precision-sensitive predictions warrant validation.
paper_title: Physical structure as an organizing principle for universal Hamiltonian learning
